game_updates.title: Update Vlog - Early Access 1.1 (Adaptive Measures)
game_updates.contents: Subnautica 2 Creative Director Anthony Gallegos is back! This time he's walking through what you can expect from our Early Access 1.1 update, Adaptive Measures, coming out tomorrow (July 8th, 2026.) He also outlines some of the features and content coming in the near future for our 1.2 update, and later in the year for Early Access 2. You can continue to speculate and discuss everything about Subnautica 2 in our official Discord server. Join the community and share your thoughts with your fellow Subnauts! You can buy Subnautica 2 on Steam now. And don’t forget to share ideas and upvote things you’d like to see in Subnautica 2 on Nolt.io. Keep Diving!

game_updates.title: v8 Build 159
game_updates.contents: This release brings a new system for adding arbitrary content (sounds, music, images, blocks, items, etc.) to maps or servers. In terms of functionality, this is very close to what JSON mods can provide, except without any manual downloads necessary. Any maps/saves with assets in them must be exported through the in-game UI to work properly; for performance reasons, assets are not embedded in map/save files unless exported in this way. This system will likely have serious bugs, so expect hotfix releases after this one. Added 'LOD-like' system for hiding various details like power lasers when zoomed out Removed rounding of camera zoom levels Optimized rendering of various static blocks (e.g. walls) Made sounds load when played instead of at game startup (saves around ~150mb of RAM) Added a ...

game_updates.title: "It's much further along than we originally planned": Fallout: London modders say work on their next game is going "swimmingly", despite DLC delays
game_updates.contents: Though Last Orders, the second DLC for massive Fallout 4 mod Fallout: London, is taking longer than Team FOLON originally planned, the modders have revealed that their next game is running ahead of schedule. The two are being worked on at the time as the group use their ambitious building of a British apocalypse atop Bethesda's Boston as a springboard into establishing themselves as a professional indie studio. game_updates.title: Slay the Spire 2 gets 15 powerful new multiplayer cards, while making life easier the first time you install a mod
game_updates.contents: Slay the Spire 2 has received a bunch of potent new cards specifically for co-operative multiplayer. They span all five of the game's classes, from the aloof and stargazing Regent to the venomous and underhand Silent (Silent! My beloved, etc). The update in question is out now via the roguelite deckbuilder's Steam beta branch, and comprises of a new colourless card, two new Regent cards, and three cards apiece for the other four classes. A few other cards have been reworked. All told, it's a great time to have friends who enjoy killing steeples. Read more

game_updates.title: Slay the Spire 2 just got 15 new cards out of nowhere, including some big co-op heavy hitters
game_updates.contents: A new Slay the Spire 2 patch has just hit the beta branch, and this is a big one. In fact, you might want to pay attention even if you aren't one to toy around with the testing side of the roguelike deckbuilder, because there's a whole heap of additional cards that are designed to enhance co-op play, and some of them sound particularly strong. There are also a bunch of fresh balance changes in the works, a shiny visual overhaul for the latest boss Aeonglass, and some modding fixes that are planned "to come to the main branch soon." Let's take a look at exactly what's in store. Read the full story on PCGamesN: Slay the Spire 2 just got 15 new cards out of nowhere, including some big co-op heavy hitters

game_updates.title: Update to Map Pool Rotation
game_updates.contents: {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40285313/bc90cd59fbe494ec79025fb5f4fc7d841353c8fd.jpg Starting today and at the start of each month, the Ranked Map pool will now automatically rotate. Each rotation will always feature a set number of open, closed, hybrid, and naval maps to keep a balanced set of maps in play at all times. This means that you'll see more varied maps more frequently in Ranked play!

game_updates.contents: Hi Adventurers,This update marks the start of the EAS9 End of Season Events.During the final stretch before the start of EAS10, the dungeons have become a more dangerous place with better rewards to match. Non-boss monsters are more aggressive.In return, dungeon drop rates have been increased across the board. Artifact drop rates have been doubled in High-Roller dungeons, and the chance to obtain better loot and higher-rarity items has increased in all dungeons. Accessory drop rates from the sub-bosses have also increased, and quest item drop rates have been boosted. This includes a small temporary chance to gain Legendary-grade quest items from PvE dungeons during this period.
